# Substrate requirement: finite-side-information-minimax-convergence

## Goal
Build axiom-clean reusable finite decision-theory substrate proving convergence from empirical finite side information to an exactly observed side-law vector.

## Provides (API contract)
- `finiteSideInfo_minimax_tendsto`: for a compact parameter space, finite labeled and nonempty side alphabets, continuous probability coordinates, and a continuous bounded real target, the bounded squared-loss minimax values based on labeled data plus `m` iid side observations tend as `m → ∞` to the benchmark minimax value based on the labeled data plus the exact side-law vector.
- A compact coordinate-simplex representation for probability mass functions on a finite type, with continuous atom coordinates and continuous finite product probabilities.
- Continuity and boundedness lemmas for finite squared risks.
- Specialization lemmas for a parameter space that is a closed subset of a finite simplex.

## Statement / milestones
Let `Theta` be compact, `X` a finite labeled alphabet, and `C` a finite nonempty side alphabet. Let `p : Theta → X → Real` and `q : Theta → C → Real` be continuous probability coordinates and let `tau : Theta → Real` be continuous and bounded. Define the bounded squared-loss minimax value when the procedure observes the labeled outcome together with `m` iid draws from `q theta`, and the benchmark value when it instead observes the exact vector `q theta`. Prove that the former tends along `Nat.atTop` to the latter.

The proof must supply the full reusable chain: exact-`q` simulation and squared-loss conditional averaging for the lower comparison; compact shrinking-fiber local-minimax convergence; finite-cover approximate decision selection measurable in the empirical side vector; a uniform finite-category empirical L1 tail from Hoeffding and a union bound; and the liminf/limsup assembly.

## Standard reference
Standard compact statistical decision theory: comparison of experiments, Rao–Blackwell conditional averaging under convex squared loss, compactness/finite-cover arguments, and finite-alphabet empirical concentration via Hoeffding. No paper-specific theorem may be assumed.

## Intended reuse
The immediate consumer is the known-marginal limiting theorem in `stat_semisupervised_discrete_ate_annotation_frontier/v1`. The shared declarations must remain paper-independent. The run-local specialization will encode its discrete-law coordinates, closed overlap-constrained model class, ATE continuity at null cells, finite-sum risks, and auxiliary empirical table.

## May assume / must derive
May assume compactness of `Theta`, finiteness/nonemptiness of the alphabets, continuity and probability-simplex validity of `p` and `q`, and continuity/boundedness of `tau`. Must derive the PMF simplex compactness/continuity API, risk continuity, shrinking-fiber minimax interchange, measurable finite-cover selector, exact-side comparison, empirical L1 concentration, and convergence theorem. All public results must have zero `sorry`, use no `admit`, and introduce no axioms.

## Non-goals (optional)
Do not import any `CausalSmith/*_Research` module. Do not encode the paper's `DiscreteLaw`, overlap inequalities, `ateFunctional`, `auxTableOf`, or annotation experiment; those are run-local prerequisites and specializations after promotion. Do not weaken the main result to a conditional gate or one-sided bound.

## Known building blocks (optional)
Search and reuse `Causalean.Stat.Minimax.FiniteSquaredLoss.Core`, `Causalean.Stat.Minimax.MinimaxValue`, `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.TailBounds.Hoeffding`, `Causalean.Stat.FiniteSquaredLoss.isCompact_procedureSet`, `Causalean.Stat.FiniteSquaredLoss.continuous_rawRisk`, `Causalean.Stat.Concentration.hoeffding_abs_ge`, `Mathlib.Probability.ProbabilityMassFunction.Constructions`, `Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.Compact`, and `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Basic`. Generic `ProbabilityTheory.minimaxRisk` and Hoeffding alone do not already provide the required compact-fiber minimax interchange.

## What to decide
1. PLACEMENT — merge-first. Find the substrate's natural topical home with `--scope module`. STRONGLY prefer MERGING each decl into an existing `Causalean/.../X.lean`; only CREATE a new topic file inside the narrowest faithful existing top-level subject area. Never invent a generic holding area. Target ≤600 lines; split before ~900 only for an independent topic/proof chain.
2. NAMESPACE — rewrite every `CausalSmith.Substrate.FiniteSideInformationMinimaxConvergence` reference to the chosen Causalean namespace (the namespace of the file it lands in).
3. REUSE / DEDUP — for each decl, search Causalean for one that already proves the SAME statement. If it exists, drop your reinvented version and use the existing one (add its import, point references at it). Reuse ONLY on genuine statement-equality — a rewire to a decl that merely looks similar will break the build. Dedup edits stay inside YOUR new content; never delete or alter an existing Causalean decl.

DOCUMENTATION (docstring-canonical) — every declaration that will render as a public library card gets a `/-- … -/` docstring whose FIRST paragraph is a self-contained natural-language translation for an econometrician with no Lean background (no Lean syntax, no field projections like `B.sigma` — say "the σ-algebra on B"; no "For every …" preamble restating the signature). This includes named local definitions or instances when the index extracts and displays them. `doc:gen` hard-fails if any published card would show “No natural-language translation yet.” Every new file opens with a `/-! … -/` module docstring stating what it provides. Theorem and lemma first paragraphs carry NL↔Lean CROSSLINKS: wrap the phrase translating each hypothesis or explicit binder in `[phrase](hyp:binderName)` (comma list `(hyp:h1,h2)` when one phrase covers several) and the conclusion phrase in `[phrase](goal)`, covering every binder and the conclusion; definition first paragraphs likewise wrap each explicit parameter's phrase in `[phrase](hyp:paramName)`, the phrase naming the defined object in `[phrase](goal)`, and the N-th given-by clause (let-step / equation alternative / conjunct) in `[phrase](step:N)`, covering every explicit parameter and the object; write the sentence to read naturally first, then bracket. `npm run lint:nl-links` is part of the integration gate and hard-fails on any incomplete or unannotated headline theorem.

The documentation gate requires every file containing a public `theorem` or `lemma` to have at least one matching declaration in `headline_theorems` in the correct `doc/library_review/<Area>.json`. Also give every NEW explorer page a short, reader-facing description: use the first paragraph of a roll-up module's `/-! ... -/` docstring when that module exists, otherwise add `namespace_intros["<path below Area>"]` to the area sidecar. Preserve every existing sidecar entry and stage the COMPLETE updated sidecar with a `write_file` op. Before output, cross-check the promoted file list and every new page path against the staged sidecar; never rely on a later failed `doc:gen` run to discover omissions.

Put the EXACT bytes you want written/inserted into each staged file (namespaced, docstringed, ready to apply).
2. Emit ONLY a small JSON manifest that REFERENCES those staged files by `from` (relative to the staging dir). It contains no code — just short paths and one short anchor line per merge, so it always parses.

`{ "ops": [ … ], "notes": "<brief rationale>" }`. `target` paths are RELATIVE to the Causalean root. Op kinds:

- `{ "kind": "create_file", "target": "Causalean/…/Foo.lean", "from": "foo.lean", "newModule": "Causalean.….Foo" }` — write the staged `from` file as a NEW file at `target`. - `{ "kind": "merge_lean", "target": "Causalean/…/X.lean", "anchor": "<a line already in X.lean>", "from": "merge_x.lean" }` — INSERT the staged `from` content after the first line containing `anchor` (empty anchor → append at end of file). INSERT-ONLY: the system preserves every existing byte and ROLLS BACK if a merge would change existing content. To add an import to an existing file, use a separate `merge_lean` anchored on an existing `import …` line (its `from` file holds just the import line). Multiple `merge_lean` ops may target the same file. If dependent inserts share one file/anchor, combine them into one staged file in dependency order, or anchor each later insert on text introduced by the prior one. Pick a SHORT, UNIQUE anchor line (a section header, a decl name) so it is unambiguous and easy to escape in JSON.
- `{ "kind": "write_file", "target": "doc/library_review/<Area>.json", "from": "area.json" }` — full-content write of a NON-Lean record file (headline sidecar, `doc/API.md`). Read the current file first, write the COMPLETE updated content to the staged `from` file (add entries/markers, never drop existing ones), and reference it here.

## Hard rules
- NEVER modify or delete an existing line in an existing Lean file. Integrating must be additive (new files + insert-only merges). If it genuinely requires editing an existing proven decl, do NOT — pick a different placement and explain in `notes`.
- Final Lean content may import and reference only Mathlib/Causalean modules. Rewrite every temporary staging reference; no `CausalSmith` import or qualified reference may remain in a staged create/merge body.
- Every `target` stays within the Causalean root; every `from` is a file you wrote under the staging dir.
- Do NOT run `lake build` / `library_index` / `embed` / `doc:gen` yourself — the system runs the full gate and rolls back on any failure. Emit only the manifest.
- Keep the manifest JSON small and valid: no code inside it, no trailing commas, all strings closed. If unsure, fewer ops with cleaner anchors.
